messages:
karen-cs: Heads-up — customer LinguaTech reports a regression in translations after today's rollout to rwd-3b-q4. They say Spanish UI now sometimes returns English answers or mixed-language fragments. Attaching examples below. :frowning:

olivia-support: They've been paying attention; said problem started ~10:30 UTC after the deploy. Customer provided request_id 01H7X2A9 and a short convo for repro.

karen-cs: Example from customer (incoming user locale=es-ES):
```
user: "¿Cuál es el horario de atención para soporte?"
api response: "Our support hours are 9am-5pm PST. Para emergencias llame al..."
```
They expect a full Spanish reply, not an English lead-in. Also another example returned partially garbled Spanish.

sam-eng: Thanks. Can you paste the exact API call (headers + model param) they used? Need to check Accept-Language, model, and model_variant. Also any prompt templates we use server-side.

karen-cs: Customer used our hosted API (v1/chat/completions) with model=rwd-3b-q4, messages system+user. Their Accept-Language header was `es-ES`. They included `x-rw-request-id: 01H7X2A9` in headers. Snippet: ```curl -H "Accept-Language: es-ES" -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -d '{"model":"rwd-3b-q4","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"¿Cuál es el horario de atención para soporte?"}]}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions``` 

mike-ml: Weird. We didn't change instruction tuning for rwd-3b-q4 today, just a kernel patch and a quantization tweak that landed in the runtime. Hypothesis: quantization path + KV-cache alignment causes language-tokenization mismatch for short prompts, resulting in partial english tokens at start. Another possibility is locale-sensitive fallback in the prompt-normalizer accidentally stripping localized system prompts on this variant. :thinking:

sam-eng: I'll pull logs for request_id 01H7X2A9 and look at model selection + token stream. If it's a runtime issue we should be able to repro on staging with the exact binary. Anyone seen similar for other regions? 

olivia-support: We also have 3 other customers in EU reporting Spanish/Portuguese mixes (HK and EU tenants). All started after the same deploy. They provided different request IDs; I'll drop them in the bug report.

deploy-bot: Deploy rwd-runtime@v2.14.7 -> prod completed by @ci at 2026-03-16T18:22:14Z. Canary passed: 95% success. (link to deploy)

mike-ml: Canary metric looked fine for token-level BLEU/chrF but those checks were English-heavy. We didn't run locale-specific regression suites for q4 variant today. I think we need quick repro + decode trace to see which tokens are being produced and where the language switch happens.

sam-eng: Action items: (1) I'll fetch logs + trace for 01H7X2A9 (2) mike, can you run a small staged job that runs the exact convo through rwd-3b-q4 with the new runtime + with the previous runtime so we can diff token outputs? (3) olivia/karen, ask customer for a minimal repro that includes raw request body and response bytes if possible. 

karen-cs: Sent a polite escalation note to LinguaTech asking for the raw response and confirming they can repro reliably. Also offered a temporary rollback to rwd-3b-q3 if needed. They accepted a rollback if we can't fix quickly. :+1:

mike-ml: I'll queue the staged run now. If we see identical outputs on previous runtime and new runtime, rule out runtime path. If it's different, probable root cause is kernel selection/quantization interplay. I'll attach decode logs here when ready.

sam-eng: Found server logs for 01H7X2A9 — model routed to rwd-3b-q4, route: chat-default, shard: g4-12. Tracing output shows early token stream starts with English tokens for "Our support" then switches. Uploading a redacted token trace to /internal/trace/01H7X2A9 (internal link). :eyes:

olivia-support: Customer replied — repro is 100% for them. They said it happens on both short prompts and some multi-turn sessions, more frequent on very short prompts.

mike-ml: Ok trace confirms language switch at token index 0-3 then Spanish tokens. That suggests a conditioning issue at generation start. Two immediate mitigation options: (A) force locale in system prompt at runtime for affected tenants, (B) roll back runtime patch. Karen/Olivia, what does customer prefer? 

karen-cs: They prefer a rollback if fix won't be quick. Asking for timeline.

sam-eng: I can stage a rollback of rwd-runtime@v2.14.6 to the affected pool within 30m if we greenlight. Need SRE approval and a short postmortem plan.

mike-ml: While rollback is in flight I'll instrument an additional check in the prompt-normalizer that preserves locale-prefixed system messages for rwd-3b-q4. That might be a hotfix we can push without full rollback.

olivia-support: I'll communicate both options to the customer. They'll wait 30m for rollback and prefer rollback first. :pray:

deploy-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-0316-01 (possible language regression after runtime patch). Assigned to @sam-eng and @mike-ml.

sam-eng: Starting rollback now. Telling SRE. Will update here once complete.

karen-cs: Thanks team. Please paste a short summary of root cause and mitigation once confirmed so I can close the escalation with the customer.

mike-ml: Will do — initial hypothesis: tokenization/quantization kernel path allowed a stray english-token bias for some prefix contexts. If confirmed we'll add locale-specific evals to the regression suite.

sam-eng: Rollback completed at 1923456890. Customer confirmed on Slack that Spanish responses look normal again. Marking as mitigated. :white_check_mark:

olivia-support: Customer very appreciative. They asked for an official postmortem and a permanent guardrail.

mike-ml: Noted. Will draft a short postmortem + remediation (locale evals + prompt-normalizer guard).
